chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about al-firāʾ, al-sammūr, al-sinjāb, foxes, and the like. He said: “There is no problem with performing salat (prayer) in it.”

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, meaning fox fur or skin used in clothing
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable or a similar fur-bearing animal mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel fur, specifically named among the materials discussed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act whose validity in such clothing is being addressed
key_terms.الْفِرَاءِ: fur garments or pelts being asked about for use in salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection; an expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in clothing made from fur such as al-sinjāb or fox?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning performing salat (prayer) in garments made from certain furs and similar materials. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no objection to praying in them, indicating permissibility in this context.
